messages.subject: minfix SPEC.md delivered (worker_status partial; 2 open items escalated)
messages.body: worker_status: partial. The spec-panel-minfix mechanism gives each finding a budget class: minor 0 words, blocking MAJOR 80 words, CRITICAL 120 words, with caps on new headings, ids, MUST-words, universal claims, conditions and check recipes; the reviser fixes by delete, then narrow, then replace, then add, and records each change in a ledger; a stdlib skill script (sc-fixcheck/fixcheck.py, run with uv run --no-project from ~/.claude/skills) diffs the snapshot against the revised spec, charges every change to a finding, reverts over-budget fixes itself, and is re-run by the next review, with brief substitution s#/sc:spec-panel @#/sc:spec-panel-minfix @# on T05/T07/T09. Predicted on S1: growth about 13% in bytes (hard ceiling 21.3%; control 63.5%; bar 44.4%), and review-3 critical+major about 3.3 (derived 2.1 to 4.0, per-replicate band about 1 to 6; control 6.0; bar 3), so the bar is a coin flip, not a safe pass. Biggest risk: a size budget cuts growth but small fixes still create blocking children (flg-r2 F12, a 58-word fix, produced N4), so review 3 may stay at 4-6 or turn fix-induced findings into unfixed escalated ones; also, the spec review hit its 3-review cap with 2 checker-scoring defects (scoring after --enforce) corrected but unreviewed, and the brainstorm debate ended blocked by 10 invariants that were carried into the merge.
